description:
'''Crank wave''' (also known as '''the post-Brexit new wave''' or '''wonk''') is a [[subgenre]] of [[post-punk]] that emerged in the mid-to late 2010s. Arising as a reaction against [[landfill indie]], acts in the genre adopted a more experimental sound, drawing variously from [[noise rock]], [[indie rock]], [[no wave]], [[krautrock]] and [[jazz fusion]]. A prominent feature is its use of [[sprechgesang]] vocals, which sit between singing and [[spoken word]]. It adopts a style of conscious lyricism and [[deadpan]] delivery.

The earliest crank wave group was Dublin's [[Gilla Band]], whose sound drew on post-punk, [[noise rock]], [[indie rock]] and [[no wave]]. The band inspired the sound to be taken up by [[Idles]], [[Fontaines D.C.]] and [[Silverbacks (band)|Silverbacks]]. The genre gained its earliest mainstream crossover in 2018 through the releases of Idles' ''[[Joy as an Act of Resistance]]'', Fontaines D.C.'s "Chequeless Reckless/Boys in The Better Land" and [[Shame (band)|Shame]]'s ''[[Songs of Praise (Shame album)|Songs of Praise]]''. The following year, Fontaines D.C.'s ''[[Dogrel]]'' and Black Midi's ''[[Schlagenheim]]'' brought the genre fully into the mainstream. The sound became particularly prominent amongst the [[Windmill scene]], a post-punk scene in south London. Around this time, [[Dan Carey (music producer)|Dan Carey]] began to produce many acts in the genre, incorporating his own influences from [[hip hop]] into their sound. During the early 2020s, a new wave of acts adopted the style including [[Yard Act]], [[Wet Leg]] and [[Squid (band)|Squid]], as its sound proliferated across the United Kingdom post-punk scene, which some publications coined "landfill Sprechgesang" or "landfill post-punk". Around 2024, crank wave began to drift from the mainstream, when major acts changed their sounds or disbanded and its place in the scene was displaced by the different sounds of [[the Last Dinner Party]] and [[Heartworms (band)|Heartworms]]. Around this time, crank wave was adopted by acts in foreign countries, particularly [[Poland]].

The category was first attested to by ''[[Louder than War]]'' editor [[John Robb (musician)|John Robb]] in May 2019, who coined it "wonk", while "crank wave" was coined in September 2019 by writer Mark Beaumont in an article for ''[[NME]]''. In 2021, writer Matthew Perpetua coined the term "the Post-Brexit New Wave" in an article for [[NPR Music]].
